subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm planning the vehicle's structure as a static six-wheeled carrier roughly 10m long and 3m wide, with a long railgun barrel mounted on top facing forward and four hydraulic outrigger legs for stabilization.

Working out the exact coordinates for wheel placement along three axles, hull dimensions, and how the stabilizer legs angle outward from the hull to ground pads between the wheel positions.

Now I'm designing the legs with nested rod sleeves and octagonal foot pads, plus a cross-brace and hydraulic piston detail, before moving to the railgun turret mounted at the rear with parallel rail boxes spaced apart with insulating gaps between them.

I'm deciding whether to give the gun a slight upward pitch for character rather than keeping it perfectly horizontal, and working out a placement helper that projects points along the gun's tilted axis so I can position capacitor rings, breech, and muzzle consistently along that angled line.

Rounding out the palette with dark armor, tan stripes, metal, warning yellow, and tire/hub tones. I'm planning the detail work: a sloped cab with glowing cyan windows, armor skirt panels with greebled vents and hazard stripes, a lathe-built radar dish, antenna rods, and capacitor bank boxes along the hull.

Now I'm working out wheel construction -- tires as 12-sided cylinders with separate hubs and manually placed lug nuts, axle rods, and fender boxes above each wheel, figuring out exact placement so wheel bottoms sit flush with the ground while legs stay braced for the deployed stance.

With that settled, I'm defining helper functions for boxes and cylinders with glow variants, then mirroring parts left/right and building the hull itself -- a lower chassis box, an upper rear deck, and a forward cab box, stacking their heights and z-offsets to form the vehicle's main body.

Tilting the windshield back slightly with a negative rotation so the top leans rearward, positioning it just ahead of the cab roof. I'm placing the cab body between z 2.4 and 4.8, adding dark blue glowing side windows near x ±1.31, a darker roof panel above, and sketching out the deck region extending from z -4.8 to 2.

Working out the turret geometry next: a ring cylinder at the pivot point, a chamfered turret body box, and a gun cradle mount above it. I'm tracing the gun barrel's origin and rail length to figure out where the muzzle ends up, checking that the barrel clears the cab roof as it angles upward toward the nose despite overhanging the cab by a couple meters.

Designing the railgun components...

Still building outrigger legs...

Now I'm positioning the fenders over each wheel so they clear the hull without overlapping, then adding wheel hubs with lug nuts arranged in a ring, plus details like headlight glow boxes and a radar dish built from a partial sphere on the cab roof.

Still adding details... exhaust stacks, antennas, tail lights, tool boxes, armor panels, camo stripes, and decal emblems across the hull and deck.

With the part count nearing 200, I'll bring in a glow kit for the wheel effects and finalize the gun's rotation and direction/normal vectors before writing the full code.
